newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. council calls for reversal of Sierra Leone coup.
newsitem.headline: U.N. council calls for reversal of Sierra Leone coup.

text.p: The Security Council on Friday called for the restoration of Sierra Leone's elected government, toppled in a May 25 coup, but refrained from endorsing the use of force advocated by West African nations.

A statement read at a council meeting said the "attempt to overthrow the democratically elected government of President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah (is) unacceptable." It called for the "immediate and unconditional restoration of constitutional order in the country."

The statement was issued after a meeting where Nigeria's foreign minister, Chief Tom Ikimi, urged the council to back an initiative by the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) calling for a combination of "dialogue, imposition of sanctions/embargo, and the use of force."
Ikimi, who was accompanied by ministers from Ghana, Guinea and Ivory Coast, said concern was expressed at an ECOWAS meeting last month about the use of force.

But he said it was "recognized that the other two options...could not be achieved without the use of military force," such as a blockade to impose sanctions and a military buildup to bolster negotiations.

The council said it was "concerned about the grave crisis in Sierra Leone which endangers the peace, security and stability of the whole region and, in particular, about its possible negative impact on the ongoing peace process in neighbouring Liberia," which is still recovering from a multi-sided civil war with the help of ECOWAS peacekeepers.

The council expressed "full support for the objectives" of ECOWAS's efforts in Sierra Leone but stopped short of endorsing all the proposed means. Ikimi later told reporters, however, that "all the elements that we would want are contained" in the council statement.

"We depart New York fully satisfied that the international community and the Security Council are in full support of the actions that we are taking as a sub-region on Sierra Leone, which has been supported fully by Africa at the summit (last month) of the OAU (Organization of African Unity)."

The council statement, which did not mention the coup leader, Major Johnny Paul Koromah, by name, referred in particular to "the atrocities committed against Sierra Leone's citizens, foreign nationals" and personnel of an ECOWAS monitoring group.
Nigerian troops were in Sierra Leone under a defence pact before the coup but have been reinforced as part of West African efforts to reinstate Kabbah.
Earlier, Secretary-General Kofi Annan backed a decision by the Commonwealth to suspend Sierra Leone until the elected government was restored.

"I hope the coup-makers in Sierra Leone will really begin to understand that the international community is not accepting what they have done and that perhaps they should begin to rethink ... and step down," he said.
